data.outcome_summary: TIMSS 2011 International Results in Mathematics reports mathematics achievement for fourth and eighth grade students across 63 countries and 14 benchmarking entities, with some countries assessing at sixth or ninth grade when needed. The assessment framework combines a content dimension (e.g., Number, Algebra, Geometry, Data and Chance) and a cognitive dimension (Knowing, Applying, Reasoning), and achievement is scaled on a 0–1000 metric with a fixed centerpoint of 500 to support trend comparisons. Each student responds to a subset of a large item pool, and achievement is summarized using scale scores, distributions, and TIMSS International Benchmarks (Advanced 625, High 550, Intermediate 475, Low 400). The report highlights cross-country differences (e.g., East Asian top performers), trends since 1995, and benchmark attainment patterns, and it also links achievement to contextual factors such as early numeracy activities, preprimary education, home resources, school composition, and instructional engagement.
